1	"""Python DSL for building circuits over the OpenQASM 2.0 subset.
2	
3	A :class:`Circuit` is created with a quantum and a classical register size
4	and extended by chaining gate and measurement methods, mirroring the
5	statements of the supported OpenQASM subset one to one::
6	
7	    circuit = Circuit(2, 2).h(0).cx(0, 1).measure(0, 0).measure(1, 1)
8	
9	Operations keep their insertion order and every chaining method returns the
10	same circuit object. The circuit renders to (:meth:`Circuit.to_qasm`) and
11	parses from (:meth:`Circuit.from_qasm`) the OpenQASM 2.0 subset text the
12	command line accepts, and simulates through the exact code paths of the
13	``simulate`` and ``probabilities`` commands (:meth:`Circuit.sample`,
14	:meth:`Circuit.probabilities`), so the returned dictionaries match the
15	commands' JSON objects field by field.
16	
17	Validation mirrors the parser's semantic rules: type mismatches raise
18	:class:`TypeError`, while out-of-range indices, non-finite angles and
19	semantic conflicts (control equal to target, repeated measurement, a gate
20	after a measurement) raise :class:`ValueError`. A rejected operation never
21	changes the circuit.
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	import math
27	
28	from .core import SimulationError, run_probabilities, run_simulation
29	from .gates import (
30	    Operation,
31	    gate_operation,
32	    gate_qasm,
33	    measurement_operation,
34	)
35	from .noise import validate_noise_model
36	from .openqasm import Program, parse
37	
38	# Register sizes accepted by the DSL match the parser's limit.
39	_MIN_REGISTER_SIZE = 1
40	_MAX_REGISTER_SIZE = 20
41	
42	_DEFAULT_SHOTS = 1024
43	_DEFAULT_SEED = 0
44	
45	
46	def _check_register_size(name: str, value: object) -> int:
47	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
48	        raise TypeError(
49	            f"{name} must be an integer, got {type(value).__name__}"
50	        )
51	    if not _MIN_REGISTER_SIZE <= value <= _MAX_REGISTER_SIZE:
52	        raise ValueError(
53	            f"{name} must be between {_MIN_REGISTER_SIZE} and {_MAX_REGISTER_SIZE}, got {value}"
54	        )
55	    return value
56	
57	
58	def _check_index(register: str, value: object, size: int) -> int:
59	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
60	        raise TypeError(
61	            f"{register} index must be an integer, got {type(value).__name__}"
62	        )
63	    if not 0 <= value < size:
64	        raise ValueError(
65	            f"{register} index {value} out of range for register of size {size}"
66	        )
67	    return value
68	
69	
70	def _check_angle(value: object) -> float:
71	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
72	        raise TypeError(
73	            f"angle must be an integer or float, got {type(value).__name__}"
74	        )
75	    angle = float(value)
76	    if not math.isfinite(angle):
77	        raise ValueError("angle must be a finite number")
78	    return angle
79	
80	
81	def _operation_line(op: Operation) -> str:
82	    """Render one operation as an OpenQASM statement (register names q/c)."""
83	    if op.kind == "measure":
84	        return f"measure q[{op.targets[0]}] -> c[{op.targets[1]}];"
85	    return gate_qasm(op.kind, op.targets, op.params[0] if op.params else None)
86	
87	
88	class Circuit:
89	    """A quantum circuit over the supported OpenQASM 2.0 subset.
90	
91	    Created with the quantum and classical register sizes (integers from 1
92	    to 20, booleans rejected) and extended through the chaining gate and
93	    measurement methods, which return the circuit itself.
94	    """
95	
96	    def __init__(self, num_qubits: int, num_clbits: int):
97	        self._num_qubits = _check_register_size("num_qubits", num_qubits)
98	        self._num_clbits = _check_register_size("num_clbits", num_clbits)
99	        self._operations: list[Operation] = []
100	        self._measured_qubits: set[int] = set()
101	        self._measured_clbits: set[int] = set()
102	        self._measurement_started = False
103	
104	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ properties
105	
106	    @property
107	    def num_qubits(self) -> int:
108	        return self._num_qubits
109	
110	    @property
111	    def num_clbits(self) -> int:
112	        return self._num_clbits
113	
114	    @property
115	    def operations(self) -> tuple[Operation, ...]:
116	        """The appended operations, in insertion order."""
117	        return tuple(self._operations)
118	
119	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
120	        return (
121	            f"Circuit(num_qubits={self._num_qubits}, num_clbits={self._num_clbits}, "
122	            f"operations={len(self._operations)})"
123	        )
124	
125	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ gates
126	
127	    def _qubit_index(self, value: object) -> int:
128	        return _check_index("qubit", value, self._num_qubits)
129	
130	    def _clbit_index(self, value: object) -> int:
131	        return _check_index("clbit", value, self._num_clbits)
132	
133	    def _check_gate_allowed(self, kind: str) -> None:
134	        if self._measurement_started:
135	            raise ValueError(f"quantum gate {kind!r} cannot be added after a measurement")
136	
137	    def _append_gate(self, op: Operation) -> Circuit:
138	        # All validation has already happened in the calling method, so a
139	        # rejected operation never reaches this point and never mutates the
140	        # circuit.
141	        self._operations.append(op)
142	        return self
143	
144	    def _fixed_single_gate(self, name: str, qubit: object) -> Circuit:
145	        target = self._qubit_index(qubit)
146	        self._check_gate_allowed(name)
147	        return self._append_gate(gate_operation(name, (target,)))
148	
149	    def _controlled_gate(self, name: str, control: object, target: object) -> Circuit:
150	        ctrl = self._qubit_index(control)
151	        tgt = self._qubit_index(target)
152	        if ctrl == tgt:
153	            raise ValueError(f"{name} control and target must be different qubits")
154	        self._check_gate_allowed(name)
155	        return self._append_gate(gate_operation(name, (ctrl, tgt)))
156	
157	    def _swap_gate(self, first: object, second: object) -> Circuit:
158	        a = self._qubit_index(first)
159	        b = self._qubit_index(second)
160	        if a == b:
161	            raise ValueError("swap operands must be different qubits")
162	        self._check_gate_allowed("swap")
163	        return self._append_gate(gate_operation("swap", (a, b)))
164	
165	    def _rotation_gate(self, name: str, angle: object, qubit: object) -> Circuit:
166	        theta = _check_angle(angle)
167	        target = self._qubit_index(qubit)
168	        self._check_gate_allowed(name)
169	        return self._append_gate(gate_operation(name, (target,), (theta,)))
170	
171	    def _controlled_rotation_gate(
172	        self, name: str, angle: object, control: object, target: object
173	    ) -> Circuit:
174	        theta = _check_angle(angle)
175	        ctrl = self._qubit_index(control)
176	        tgt = self._qubit_index(target)
177	        if ctrl == tgt:
178	            raise ValueError(f"{name} control and target must be different qubits")
179	        self._check_gate_allowed(name)
180	        return self._append_gate(gate_operation(name, (ctrl, tgt), (theta,)))
181	
182	    def x(self, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
183	        """Append an ``x`` gate on *qubit*."""
184	        return self._fixed_single_gate("x", qubit)
185	
186	    def h(self, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
187	        """Append an ``h`` gate on *qubit*."""
188	        return self._fixed_single_gate("h", qubit)
189	
190	    def y(self, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
191	        """Append a ``y`` gate on *qubit*."""
192	        return self._fixed_single_gate("y", qubit)
193	
194	    def z(self, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
195	        """Append a ``z`` gate on *qubit*."""
196	        return self._fixed_single_gate("z", qubit)
197	
198	    def s(self, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
199	        """Append an ``s`` gate on *qubit*."""
200	        return self._fixed_single_gate("s", qubit)
201	
202	    def sdg(self, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
203	        """Append an ``sdg`` gate on *qubit*."""
204	        return self._fixed_single_gate("sdg", qubit)
205	
206	    def t(self, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
207	        """Append a ``t`` gate on *qubit*."""
208	        return self._fixed_single_gate("t", qubit)
209	
210	    def tdg(self, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
211	        """Append a ``tdg`` gate on *qubit*."""
212	        return self._fixed_single_gate("tdg", qubit)
213	
214	    def cx(self, control: int, target: int) -> Circuit:
215	        """Append a ``cx`` gate from *control* to *target*."""
216	        return self._controlled_gate("cx", control, target)
217	
218	    def cz(self, control: int, target: int) -> Circuit:
219	        """Append a ``cz`` gate from *control* to *target*."""
220	        return self._controlled_gate("cz", control, target)
221	
222	    def swap(self, first: int, second: int) -> Circuit:
223	        """Append a ``swap`` gate exchanging *first* and *second*."""
224	        return self._swap_gate(first, second)
225	
226	    def rx(self, angle: float, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
227	        """Append an ``rx(angle)`` gate on *qubit* (angle in radians)."""
228	        return self._rotation_gate("rx", angle, qubit)
229	
230	    def ry(self, angle: float, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
231	        """Append an ``ry(angle)`` gate on *qubit* (angle in radians)."""
232	        return self._rotation_gate("ry", angle, qubit)
233	
234	    def rz(self, angle: float, qubit: int) -> Circuit:
235	        """Append an ``rz(angle)`` gate on *qubit* (angle in radians)."""
236	        return self._rotation_gate("rz", angle, qubit)
237	
238	    def crx(self, angle: float, control: int, target: int) -> Circuit:
239	        """Append a ``crx(angle)`` gate from *control* to *target*."""
240	        return self._controlled_rotation_gate("crx", angle, control, target)
241	
242	    def cry(self, angle: float, control: int, target: int) -> Circuit:
243	        """Append a ``cry(angle)`` gate from *control* to *target*."""
244	        return self._controlled_rotation_gate("cry", angle, control, target)
245	
246	    def crz(self, angle: float, control: int, target: int) -> Circuit:
247	        """Append a ``crz(angle)`` gate from *control* to *target*."""
248	        return self._controlled_rotation_gate("crz", angle, control, target)
249	
250	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ measurement
251	
252	    def measure(self, qubit: int, clbit: int) -> Circuit:
253	        """Append ``measure qubit -> clbit``.
254	
255	        Each qubit and each clbit may take part in at most one measurement,
256	        and no quantum gate may be added once measurement has started.
257	        """
258	        q = self._qubit_index(qubit)
259	        c = self._clbit_index(clbit)
260	        if q in self._measured_qubits:
261	            raise ValueError(f"qubit {q} is measured more than once")
262	        if c in self._measured_clbits:
263	            raise ValueError(f"clbit {c} is the target of more than one measurement")
264	        self._measured_qubits.add(q)
265	        self._measured_clbits.add(c)
266	        self._measurement_started = True
267	        self._operations.append(measurement_operation(q, c))
268	        return self
269	
270	    # --------------------------------------------------------------- OpenQASM
271	
272	    def to_qasm(self) -> str:
273	        """Render the circuit as OpenQASM 2.0 subset text.
274	
275	        Uses the fixed register names ``q`` and ``c``, emits the operations
276	        in insertion order with the same statement semantics as the parser,
277	        and ends with a trailing newline. Angles use the shortest decimal
278	        representation that round-trips to the same float (negative zero is
279	        written as ``0``).
280	        """
281	        lines = [
282	            "OPENQASM 2.0;",
283	            'include "qelib1.inc";',
284	            f"qreg q[{self._num_qubits}];",
285	            f"creg c[{self._num_clbits}];",
286	        ]
287	        lines.extend(_operation_line(op) for op in self._operations)
288	        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
289	
290	    @classmethod
291	    def from_qasm(cls, source: str) -> Circuit:
292	        """Build a circuit from OpenQASM 2.0 subset text.
293	
294	        Parsing and validation are exactly those of the command line:
295	        :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.ParseError` and
296	        :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.ValidationError` propagate with
297	        their 1-based line/column positions intact.
298	        """
299	        if not isinstance(source, str):
300	            raise TypeError(f"source must be a string, got {type(source).__name__}")
301	        program = parse(source)
302	        circuit = cls(program.num_qubits, program.num_clbits)
303	        for op in program.operations:
304	            # The program is fully validated, so these invariants hold.
305	            if op.kind == "measure":
306	                circuit._measured_qubits.add(op.targets[0])
307	                circuit._measured_clbits.add(op.targets[1])
308	                circuit._measurement_started = True
309	            circuit._operations.append(op)
310	        return circuit
311	
312	    # -------------------------------------------------------------- simulation
313	
314	    def _to_program(self) -> Program:
315	        return Program(self._num_qubits, self._num_clbits, tuple(self._operations))
316	
317	    @staticmethod
318	    def _prepare_noise_model(noise_model: object) -> dict[str, float] | None:
319	        if noise_model is None:
320	            return None
321	        return validate_noise_model(noise_model)
322	
323	    def sample(self, shots: int = _DEFAULT_SHOTS, seed: int = _DEFAULT_SEED, noise_model=None) -> dict:
324	        """Sample the circuit, returning the ``simulate`` payload as a dict.
325	
326	        The result equals the JSON object the ``simulate`` command produces
327	        for :meth:`to_qasm` with the same *shots*, *seed* and noise model
328	        (defaults 1024 and 0). *noise_model* is a mapping with the four
329	        optional channels; invalid models raise
330	        :class:`~quantum_circuit.noise.NoiseModelError`. Each call samples
331	        from a fresh RNG seeded by *seed*, so repeated calls with equal
332	        arguments return equal results and no random state is shared. The
333	        circuit itself is never modified.
334	        """
335	        if isinstance(shots, bool) or not isinstance(shots, int):
336	            raise TypeError(f"shots must be an integer, got {type(shots).__name__}")
337	        if shots <= 0:
338	            raise ValueError(f"shots must be a positive integer, got {shots}")
339	        if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
340	            raise TypeError(f"seed must be an integer, got {type(seed).__name__}")
341	        model = self._prepare_noise_model(noise_model)
342	        program = self._to_program()
343	        try:
344	            return run_simulation(program, shots, seed, model)
345	        except SimulationError as exc:
346	            # The DSL reports the noisy size limit as a ValueError, matching
347	            # its other value-range errors rather than the CLI's exit code 3.
348	            raise ValueError(str(exc)) from None
349	
350	    def probabilities(self, noise_model=None) -> dict:
351	        """Exact final-state measurement probabilities, as a dict.
352	
353	        The result equals the JSON object the ``probabilities`` command
354	        produces for :meth:`to_qasm` with the same noise model. The circuit
355	        itself is never modified.
356	        """
357	        model = self._prepare_noise_model(noise_model)
358	        program = self._to_program()
359	        try:
360	            return run_probabilities(program, model)
361	        except SimulationError as exc:
362	            raise ValueError(str(exc)) from None
363	
364	
365	__all__ = ["Circuit"]

1	"""Lexer, parser and semantic validation for the OpenQASM 2.0 subset.
2	
3	Supported subset::
4	
5	    OPENQASM 2.0;
6	    include "qelib1.inc";
7	    qreg name[positive-size];
8	    creg name[positive-size];
9	    x qubit;
10	    h qubit;
11	    y qubit;
12	    z qubit;
13	    s qubit;
14	    sdg qubit;
15	    t qubit;
16	    tdg qubit;
17	    cx qubit, qubit;
18	    cz qubit, qubit;
19	    swap qubit, qubit;
20	    rx(angle) qubit;
21	    ry(angle) qubit;
22	    rz(angle) qubit;
23	    crx(angle) qubit, qubit;
24	    cry(angle) qubit, qubit;
25	    crz(angle) qubit, qubit;
26	    measure qubit -> cbit;
27	
28	Only one ``qreg`` and one ``creg`` may be declared, and gates/measures only
29	accept single bits with constant integer indices. Line comments (``//``) are
30	supported.
31	
32	Angle expressions are written in radians and may use decimal integer and
33	real literals (including scientific notation), the constant ``pi``,
34	parentheses, unary ``+``/``-`` and the binary operators ``+``, ``-``, ``*``
35	and ``/`` with the usual precedence (``*``/``/`` before ``+``/``-``, same
36	precedence evaluated left to right, parentheses first).
37	"""
38	
39	from __future__ import annotations
40	
41	import math
42	from dataclasses import dataclass
43	
44	from .gates import (
45	    CONTROLLED,
46	    GATE_SPECS,
47	    SWAP,
48	    Operation,
49	    gate_operation,
50	    measurement_operation,
51	)
52	
53	# Re-exported so modules that already import the validated operation type
54	# from the parser module keep working; the definition itself lives with the
55	# authoritative gate semantics in :mod:`quantum_circuit.gates`.
56	__all__ = ["ParseError", "ValidationError", "Token", "Operation", "Program", "parse", "tokenize"]
57	
58	
59	class ParseError(Exception):
60	    """A lexical or syntactic problem (reported as ``parse_error``)."""
61	
62	    def __init__(self, message: str, line: int, column: int):
63	        super().__init__(message)
64	        self.message = message
65	        self.line = line
66	        self.column = column
67	
68	
69	class ValidationError(Exception):
70	    """A syntactically valid but semantically invalid program."""
71	
72	    def __init__(self, message: str, line: int, column: int):
73	        super().__init__(message)
74	        self.message = message
75	        self.line = line
76	        self.column = column
77	
78	
79	@dataclass(frozen=True)
80	class Token:
81	    kind: str  # 'ident', 'int', 'real', 'string' or a literal punctuation word
82	    value: str
83	    line: int  # 1-based
84	    column: int  # 1-based, points at the first character of the token
85	
86	
87	_KEYWORDS = {"OPENQASM", "include", "qreg", "creg", "measure"}
88	# Gate names, operand shapes and parameter rules all come from the single
89	# semantic registry in :mod:`quantum_circuit.gates`.
90	_BUILTIN_GATES = frozenset(GATE_SPECS)
91	
92	# A state vector has 2**n amplitudes; larger registers cannot be simulated
93	# and are rejected as illegal sizes rather than crashing.
94	_MAX_REGISTER_SIZE = 20
95	
96	
97	def tokenize(source: str) -> list[Token]:
98	    """Split *source* into tokens.
99	
100	    Raises :class:`ParseError` (with 1-based position) on invalid input.
101	    """
102	    tokens: list[Token] = []
103	    line = 1
104	    col = 1
105	    n = len(source)
106	    i = 0
107	
108	    while i < n:
109	        ch = source[i]
110	
111	        if ch == "\n":
112	            i += 1
113	            line += 1
114	            col = 1
115	            continue
116	        if ch in " \t\r":
117	            i += 1
118	            col += 1
119	            continue
120	
121	        # Line comment: runs to end of line (end of input also terminates it).
122	        if ch == "/" and i + 1 < n and source[i + 1] == "/":
123	            i += 2
124	            col += 2
125	            while i < n and source[i] != "\n":
126	                i += 1
127	                col += 1
128	            continue
129	
130	        start_line, start_col = line, col
131	
132	        if ch.isalpha() or ch == "_":
133	            j = i + 1
134	            while j < n and (source[j].isalnum() or source[j] == "_"):
135	                j += 1
136	            word = source[i:j]
137	            kind = word if word in _KEYWORDS else "ident"
138	            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
139	            col += j - i
140	            i = j
141	            continue
142	
143	        if ch.isdigit() or (ch == "." and i + 1 < n and source[i + 1].isdigit()):
144	            j = i
145	            seen_dot = False
146	            seen_exp = False
147	            while j < n:
148	                c = source[j]
149	                if c.isdigit():
150	                    j += 1
151	                elif c == "." and not seen_dot and not seen_exp:
152	                    seen_dot = True
153	                    j += 1
154	                elif c in "eE" and not seen_exp:
155	                    seen_exp = True
156	                    j += 1
157	                    if j < n and source[j] in "+-":
158	                        j += 1
159	                else:
160	                    break
161	            word = source[i:j]
162	            kind = "real" if seen_dot or seen_exp else "int"
163	            tokens.append(Token(kind, word, start_line, start_col))
164	            col += j - i
165	            i = j
166	            continue
167	
168	        if ch == '"':
169	            j = i + 1
170	            while j < n and source[j] != '"':
171	                if source[j] == "\n":
172	                    raise ParseError("unterminated string literal", start_line, start_col)
173	                j += 1
174	            if j >= n:
175	                raise ParseError("unterminated string literal", start_line, start_col)
176	            tokens.append(Token("string", source[i + 1 : j], start_line, start_col))
177	            col += j - i + 1
178	            i = j + 1
179	            continue
180	
181	        if ch == "-" and i + 1 < n and source[i + 1] == ">":
182	            tokens.append(Token("->", "->", start_line, start_col))
183	            i += 2
184	            col += 2
185	            continue
186	
187	        if ch in "[];,()+*/-":
188	            tokens.append(Token(ch, ch, start_line, start_col))
189	            i += 1
190	            col += 1
191	            continue
192	
193	        raise ParseError(f"unexpected character {ch!r}", start_line, start_col)
194	
195	    tokens.append(Token("eof", "", line, col))
196	    return tokens
197	
198	
199	@dataclass(frozen=True)
200	class Program:
201	    num_qubits: int
202	    num_clbits: int
203	    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]
204	
205	
206	def _parse_decimal(token: Token) -> int:
207	    """Parse a non-negative decimal literal, rejecting oversized ones."""
208	    if len(token.value) > 18:
209	        raise ValidationError("integer literal is too large", token.line, token.column)
210	    return int(token.value)
211	
212	
213	def parse(source: str) -> Program:
214	    """Parse and validate the OpenQASM subset, returning a :class:`Program`."""
215	    tokens = tokenize(source)
216	    pos = 0
217	
218	    def peek() -> Token:
219	        return tokens[pos]
220	
221	    def advance() -> Token:
222	        nonlocal pos
223	        tok = tokens[pos]
224	        pos += 1
225	        return tok
226	
227	    def expect(kind: str) -> Token:
228	        tok = peek()
229	        if tok.kind != kind:
230	            raise ParseError(f"expected {kind!r} but found {tok.value!r}", tok.line, tok.column)
231	        return advance()
232	
233	    # Header: OPENQASM 2.0;  (a real token "2.0", exactly)
234	    first = peek()
235	    if first.kind != "OPENQASM":
236	        raise ParseError("expected 'OPENQASM' declaration", first.line, first.column)
237	    advance()
238	    version = expect("real") if peek().kind == "real" else expect("int")
239	    if version.value != "2.0":
240	        raise ParseError(f"unsupported OpenQASM version {version.value!r}", version.line, version.column)
241	    expect(";")
242	
243	    # Exactly: include "qelib1.inc";
244	    expect("include")
245	    path = expect("string")
246	    if path.value != "qelib1.inc":
247	        raise ValidationError(f"unknown include file {path.value!r}", path.line, path.column)
248	    expect(";")
249	
250	    qreg_name: str | None = None
251	    qreg_size: int | None = None
252	    creg_name: str | None = None
253	    creg_size: int | None = None
254	    operations: list[Operation] = []
255	    measured_qubits: set[int] = set()
256	    measured_clbits: set[int] = set()
257	    measurement_started = False
258	
259	    def parse_index(reg_kind: str) -> tuple[int, Token, Token]:
260	        """Parse ``name[const]`` returning (index, name token, index token)."""
261	        name_tok = expect("ident")
262	        expect("[")
263	        idx_tok = expect("int")
264	        expect("]")
265	        if reg_kind == "q":
266	            if name_tok.value != qreg_name:
267	                if creg_name is not None and name_tok.value == creg_name:
268	                    raise ValidationError(
269	                        "classical register used where a quantum register is required",
270	                        name_tok.line,
271	                        name_tok.column,
272	                    )
273	                raise ValidationError(
274	                    f"undeclared quantum register {name_tok.value!r}",
275	                    name_tok.line,
276	                    name_tok.column,
277	                )
278	            size = qreg_size
279	        else:
280	            if name_tok.value != creg_name:
281	                if qreg_name is not None and name_tok.value == qreg_name:
282	                    raise ValidationError(
283	                        "quantum register used where a classical register is required",
284	                        name_tok.line,
285	                        name_tok.column,
286	                    )
287	                raise ValidationError(
288	                    f"undeclared classical register {name_tok.value!r}",
289	                    name_tok.line,
290	                    name_tok.column,
291	                )
292	            size = creg_size
293	        idx = _parse_decimal(idx_tok)
294	        assert size is not None
295	        if not 0 <= idx < size:
296	            raise ValidationError(
297	                f"register index {idx} out of range for register of size {size}",
298	                idx_tok.line,
299	                idx_tok.column,
300	            )
301	        return idx, name_tok, idx_tok
302	
303	    def parse_angle() -> float:
304	        """Parse and evaluate an angle expression (result in radians).
305	
306	        Grammar (usual precedence, left associativity, parentheses first)::
307	
308	            expr    := term (('+' | '-') term)*
309	            term    := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
310	            factor  := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
311	            atom    := int | real | 'pi' | '(' expr ')'
312	        """
313	
314	        def check_finite(value: float, op_tok: Token) -> float:
315	            if not math.isfinite(value):
316	                raise ValidationError(
317	                    "angle expression result is not a finite number",
318	                    op_tok.line,
319	                    op_tok.column,
320	                )
321	            return value
322	
323	        def parse_atom() -> float:
324	            tok = peek()
325	            if tok.kind == "int":
326	                advance()
327	                return float(_parse_decimal(tok))
328	            if tok.kind == "real":
329	                advance()
330	                try:
331	                    value = float(tok.value)
332	                except ValueError:
333	                    raise ParseError(
334	                        f"malformed numeric literal {tok.value!r}",
335	                        tok.line,
336	                        tok.column,
337	                    ) from None
338	                if not math.isfinite(value):
339	                    raise ValidationError(
340	                        f"numeric literal {tok.value!r} is too large",
341	                        tok.line,
342	                        tok.column,
343	                    )
344	                return value
345	            if tok.kind == "ident":
346	                advance()
347	                if tok.value == "pi":
348	                    return math.pi
349	                raise ValidationError(
350	                    f"unknown name {tok.value!r} in angle expression",
351	                    tok.line,
352	                    tok.column,
353	                )
354	            if tok.kind == "(":
355	                advance()
356	                value = parse_expr()
357	                expect(")")
358	                return value
359	            raise ParseError(
360	                f"expected a number, 'pi' or '(' but found {tok.value!r}",
361	                tok.line,
362	                tok.column,
363	            )
364	
365	        def parse_factor() -> float:
366	            tok = peek()
367	            if tok.kind == "+" or tok.kind == "-":
368	                advance()
369	                operand = parse_factor()
370	                return operand if tok.kind == "+" else -operand
371	            return parse_atom()
372	
373	        def parse_term() -> float:
374	            value = parse_factor()
375	            while peek().kind == "*" or peek().kind == "/":
376	                op_tok = advance()
377	                rhs = parse_factor()
378	                if op_tok.kind == "*":
379	                    value = check_finite(value * rhs, op_tok)
380	                else:
381	                    if rhs == 0.0:
382	                        raise ValidationError(
383	                            "division by zero in angle expression",
384	                            op_tok.line,
385	                            op_tok.column,
386	                        )
387	                    value = check_finite(value / rhs, op_tok)
388	            return value
389	
390	        def parse_expr() -> float:
391	            value = parse_term()
392	            while peek().kind == "+" or peek().kind == "-":
393	                op_tok = advance()
394	                rhs = parse_term()
395	                if op_tok.kind == "+":
396	                    value = check_finite(value + rhs, op_tok)
397	                else:
398	                    value = check_finite(value - rhs, op_tok)
399	            return value
400	
401	        return parse_expr()
402	
403	    while peek().kind != "eof":
404	        tok = peek()
405	
406	        if tok.kind == "qreg" or tok.kind == "creg":
407	            advance()
408	            is_qreg = tok.kind == "qreg"
409	            name_tok = expect("ident")
410	            expect("[")
411	            size_tok = expect("int")
412	            expect("]")
413	            expect(";")
414	            size = _parse_decimal(size_tok)
415	            if not 1 <= size <= _MAX_REGISTER_SIZE:
416	                raise ValidationError(
417	                    f"register size must be between 1 and {_MAX_REGISTER_SIZE}, got {size}",
418	                    size_tok.line,
419	                    size_tok.column,
420	                )
421	            if is_qreg:
422	                if qreg_name is not None:
423	                    raise ValidationError(
424	                        "duplicate declaration of quantum register",
425	                        name_tok.line,
426	                        name_tok.column,
427	                    )
428	                if creg_name is not None and name_tok.value == creg_name:
429	                    raise ValidationError(
430	                        f"register name {name_tok.value!r} already declared",
431	                        name_tok.line,
432	                        name_tok.column,
433	                    )
434	                qreg_name = name_tok.value
435	                qreg_size = size
436	            else:
437	                if creg_name is not None:
438	                    raise ValidationError(
439	                        "duplicate declaration of classical register",
440	                        name_tok.line,
441	                        name_tok.column,
442	                    )
443	                if qreg_name is not None and name_tok.value == qreg_name:
444	                    raise ValidationError(
445	                        f"register name {name_tok.value!r} already declared",
446	                        name_tok.line,
447	                        name_tok.column,
448	                    )
449	                creg_name = name_tok.value
450	                creg_size = size
451	            continue
452	
453	        if tok.kind == "measure":
454	            advance()
455	            q_idx, q_name_tok, _q_idx_tok = parse_index("q")
456	            expect("->")
457	            c_idx, c_name_tok, _c_idx_tok = parse_index("c")
458	            expect(";")
459	            if q_idx in measured_qubits:
460	                raise ValidationError(
461	                    f"qubit {qreg_name}[{q_idx}] is measured more than once",
462	                    q_name_tok.line,
463	                    q_name_tok.column,
464	                )
465	            if c_idx in measured_clbits:
466	                raise ValidationError(
467	                    f"clbit {creg_name}[{c_idx}] is the target of more than one measurement",
468	                    c_name_tok.line,
469	                    c_name_tok.column,
470	                )
471	            measured_qubits.add(q_idx)
472	            measured_clbits.add(c_idx)
473	            measurement_started = True
474	            operations.append(measurement_operation(q_idx, c_idx))
475	            continue
476	
477	        if tok.kind == "ident":
478	            gate_name = tok.value
479	            if gate_name not in _BUILTIN_GATES:
480	                raise ValidationError(
481	                    f"undeclared identifier or unsupported gate {gate_name!r}",
482	                    tok.line,
483	                    tok.column,
484	                )
485	            if measurement_started:
486	                raise ValidationError(
487	                    f"quantum gate {gate_name!r} appears after a measurement",
488	                    tok.line,
489	                    tok.column,
490	                )
491	            advance()
492	            spec = GATE_SPECS[gate_name]
493	            if spec.parameterized:
494	                expect("(")
495	                angle = parse_angle()
496	                if peek().kind == ",":
497	                    comma = peek()
498	                    raise ParseError(
499	                        f"gate {gate_name!r} takes exactly one angle parameter",
500	                        comma.line,
501	                        comma.column,
502	                    )
503	                expect(")")
504	            if spec.style == CONTROLLED:
505	                ctrl, _, _ = parse_index("q")
506	                expect(",")
507	                tgt, tgt_name_tok, _ = parse_index("q")
508	                expect(";")
509	                if ctrl == tgt:
510	                    raise ValidationError(
511	                        f"{gate_name} control and target must be different qubits",
512	                        tgt_name_tok.line,
513	                        tgt_name_tok.column,
514	                    )
515	                targets = (ctrl, tgt)
516	            elif spec.style == SWAP:
517	                first, _, _ = parse_index("q")
518	                expect(",")
519	                second, second_name_tok, _ = parse_index("q")
520	                expect(";")
521	                if first == second:
522	                    raise ValidationError(
523	                        f"{gate_name} operands must be different qubits",
524	                        second_name_tok.line,
525	                        second_name_tok.column,
526	                    )
527	                targets = (first, second)
528	            else:
529	                target, _, _ = parse_index("q")
530	                expect(";")
531	                targets = (target,)
532	            params = (angle,) if spec.parameterized else ()
533	            operations.append(gate_operation(gate_name, targets, params))
534	            continue
535	
536	        raise ParseError(
537	            f"unexpected token {tok.value!r}",
538	            tok.line,
539	            tok.column,
540	        )
541	
542	    eof = peek()
543	    if qreg_name is None:
544	        raise ValidationError("missing required quantum register declaration", eof.line, eof.column)
545	    if creg_name is None:
546	        raise ValidationError("missing required classical register declaration", eof.line, eof.column)
547	
548	    return Program(
549	        num_qubits=qreg_size if qreg_size is not None else 0,
550	        num_clbits=creg_size if creg_size is not None else 0,
551	        operations=tuple(operations),
552	    )

1	"""Density-matrix simulation with configurable noise channels.
2	
3	Enabled via ``simulate --noise-model PATH``. The model is a JSON object with
4	up to four channel keys (probabilities in ``[0, 1]``):
5	
6	- ``amplitude_damping``: |1> decays to |0> with probability gamma.
7	- ``phase_damping``: populations unchanged, off-diagonal entries scaled by
8	  ``1 - gamma``.
9	- ``bit_flip``: ``rho -> (1 - p) rho + p X rho X``.
10	- ``depolarizing``: ``rho -> (1 - p) rho + p I/2`` (the qubit is replaced by
11	  the maximally mixed state with probability ``p``).
12	
13	After every quantum gate, each configured channel is applied to every qubit
14	the gate touched. Qubits of a two-qubit gate (``cx``, ``cz``, ``crx``,
15	``cry``, ``crz``, ``swap``) are processed in ascending index order; channels
16	on one qubit are applied in :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER` order.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import json
22	import math
23	from collections.abc import Mapping
24	
25	from .gates import (
26	    controlled_target_unitary,
27	    single_qubit_unitary,
28	)
29	from .openqasm import Program
30	
31	# Fixed order in which channels are applied per qubit and echoed back.
32	CHANNEL_ORDER = ("amplitude_damping", "phase_damping", "bit_flip", "depolarizing")
33	
34	# A density matrix holds 4**n entries, so noisy simulation is capped well
35	# below the state-vector register limit.
36	MAX_NOISE_QUBITS = 10
37	
38	
39	class NoiseModelError(Exception):
40	    """The noise model content is invalid (reported as ``noise_model_error``)."""
41	
42	
43	def _reject_constant(value: str) -> None:
44	    # json accepts NaN/Infinity by default; they are not valid JSON numbers.
45	    raise NoiseModelError(f"noise model contains non-JSON constant {value!r}")
46	
47	
48	def _object_pairs(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict[str, object]:
49	    result: dict[str, object] = {}
50	    for key, value in pairs:
51	        if key in result:
52	            raise NoiseModelError(f"duplicate key {key!r} in noise model")
53	        result[key] = value
54	    return result
55	
56	
57	def parse_noise_model(text: str) -> dict[str, float]:
58	    """Parse and validate noise-model JSON text.
59	
60	    Returns the configured channels as a mapping in :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER`
61	    order with float probabilities, so models differing only in whitespace
62	    or key order produce identical output. Raises :class:`NoiseModelError`
63	    on any invalid content.
64	    """
65	    try:
66	        data = json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=_object_pairs, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
67	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
68	        raise NoiseModelError(f"noise model is not valid JSON: {exc}") from None
69	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
70	        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must be a JSON object")
71	    if not data:
72	        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must configure at least one channel")
73	    for key, value in data.items():
74	        if key not in CHANNEL_ORDER:
75	            raise NoiseModelError(f"unknown noise channel {key!r}")
76	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
77	            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be a JSON number")
78	        probability = float(value)
79	        if not math.isfinite(probability):
80	            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be finite")
81	        if not 0.0 <= probability <= 1.0:
82	            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be between 0 and 1")
83	    return {channel: float(data[channel]) for channel in CHANNEL_ORDER if channel in data}
84	
85	
86	def validate_noise_model(model: object) -> dict[str, float]:
87	    """Validate a noise model given directly as a mapping (the Python DSL).
88	
89	    Applies the same channel and probability rules as
90	    :func:`parse_noise_model` and returns the same canonical mapping in
91	    :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER` order with float probabilities, so a model passed
92	    as a Python mapping behaves exactly like the equivalent JSON file.
93	    Raises :class:`NoiseModelError` on any invalid content.
94	    """
95	    if isinstance(model, bool) or not isinstance(model, Mapping):
96	        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must be a mapping of channel names to probabilities")
97	    if not model:
98	        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must configure at least one channel")
99	    for key, value in model.items():
100	        if not isinstance(key, str) or key not in CHANNEL_ORDER:
101	            raise NoiseModelError(f"unknown noise channel {key!r}")
102	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
103	            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be a number")
104	        probability = float(value)
105	        if not math.isfinite(probability):

"""Density-matrix simulation with configurable noise channels.

Enabled via ``simulate --noise-model PATH``. The model is a JSON object with
up to four channel keys (probabilities in ``[0, 1]``):

- ``amplitude_damping``: |1> decays to |0> with probability gamma.
- ``phase_damping``: populations unchanged, off-diagonal entries scaled by
  ``1 - gamma``.
- ``bit_flip``: ``rho -> (1 - p) rho + p X rho X``.
- ``depolarizing``: ``rho -> (1 - p) rho + p I/2`` (the qubit is replaced by
  the maximally mixed state with probability ``p``).

After every quantum gate, each configured channel is applied to every qubit
the gate touched. Qubits of a two-qubit gate (``cx``, ``cz``, ``crx``,
``cry``, ``crz``, ``swap``) are processed in ascending index order; channels
on one qubit are applied in :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER` order.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
from collections.abc import Mapping

from .gates import (
    controlled_target_unitary,
    single_qubit_unitary,
)
from .openqasm import Program

# Fixed order in which channels are applied per qubit and echoed back.
CHANNEL_ORDER = ("amplitude_damping", "phase_damping", "bit_flip", "depolarizing")

# A density matrix holds 4**n entries, so noisy simulation is capped well
# below the state-vector register limit.
MAX_NOISE_QUBITS = 10


class NoiseModelError(Exception):
    """The noise model content is invalid (reported as ``noise_model_error``)."""


def _reject_constant(value: str) -> None:
    # json accepts NaN/Infinity by default; they are not valid JSON numbers.
    raise NoiseModelError(f"noise model contains non-JSON constant {value!r}")


def _object_pairs(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict[str, object]:
    result: dict[str, object] = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise NoiseModelError(f"duplicate key {key!r} in noise model")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def parse_noise_model(text: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Parse and validate noise-model JSON text.

    Returns the configured channels as a mapping in :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER`
    order with float probabilities, so models differing only in whitespace
    or key order produce identical output. Raises :class:`NoiseModelError`
    on any invalid content.
    """
    try:
        data = json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=_object_pairs, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise NoiseModelError(f"noise model is not valid JSON: {exc}") from None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must be a JSON object")
    if not data:
        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must configure at least one channel")
    for key, value in data.items():
        if key not in CHANNEL_ORDER:
            raise NoiseModelError(f"unknown noise channel {key!r}")
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be a JSON number")
        probability = float(value)
        if not math.isfinite(probability):
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be finite")
        if not 0.0 <= probability <= 1.0:
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be between 0 and 1")
    return {channel: float(data[channel]) for channel in CHANNEL_ORDER if channel in data}


def validate_noise_model(model: object) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Validate a noise model given directly as a mapping (the Python DSL).

    Applies the same channel and probability rules as
    :func:`parse_noise_model` and returns the same canonical mapping in
    :data:`CHANNEL_ORDER` order with float probabilities, so a model passed
    as a Python mapping behaves exactly like the equivalent JSON file.
    Raises :class:`NoiseModelError` on any invalid content.
    """
    if isinstance(model, bool) or not isinstance(model, Mapping):
        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must be a mapping of channel names to probabilities")
    if not model:
        raise NoiseModelError("noise model must configure at least one channel")
    for key, value in model.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or key not in CHANNEL_ORDER:
            raise NoiseModelError(f"unknown noise channel {key!r}")
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be a number")
        probability = float(value)
        if not math.isfinite(probability):
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be finite")
        if not 0.0 <= probability <= 1.0:
            raise NoiseModelError(f"noise channel {key!r} probability must be between 0 and 1")
    return {channel: float(model[channel]) for channel in CHANNEL_ORDER if channel in model}


def _basis_offsets(size: int, bit: int):
    """Yield indices below *size* whose ``bit`` is clear, block by block."""
    step = bit << 1
    for base in range(0, size, step):
        yield from range(base, base + bit)


def _apply_single_qubit(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, matrix) -> None:
    """Apply ``rho -> U rho U†`` for a single-qubit unitary ``U``."""
    bit = 1 << qubit
    g00, g01, g10, g11 = matrix
    h00, h01 = g00.conjugate(), g01.conjugate()
    h10, h11 = g10.conjugate(), g11.conjugate()
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            m00 = row0[j0]
            m01 = row0[j1]
            m10 = row1[j0]
            m11 = row1[j1]
            t00 = g00 * m00 + g01 * m10
            t01 = g00 * m01 + g01 * m11
            t10 = g10 * m00 + g11 * m10
            t11 = g10 * m01 + g11 * m11
            row0[j0] = t00 * h00 + t01 * h01
            row0[j1] = t00 * h10 + t01 * h11
            row1[j0] = t10 * h00 + t11 * h01
            row1[j1] = t10 * h10 + t11 * h11


def _apply_cx(rho: list[list[complex]], control: int, target: int, size: int) -> None:
    """Apply the cx basis permutation to both axes of the density matrix."""
    cbit = 1 << control
    tbit = 1 << target
    swapped = [i for i in range(size) if (i & cbit) and not (i & tbit)]
    for i in swapped:
        j = i | tbit
        rho[i], rho[j] = rho[j], rho[i]
    for i in swapped:
        j = i | tbit
        for row in rho:
            row[i], row[j] = row[j], row[i]


def _apply_swap(rho: list[list[complex]], first: int, second: int, size: int) -> None:
    """Apply the swap basis permutation to both axes of the density matrix."""
    first_bit = 1 << first
    second_bit = 1 << second
    swapped = [i for i in range(size) if (i & first_bit) and not (i & second_bit)]
    for i in swapped:
        j = (i ^ first_bit) | second_bit
        rho[i], rho[j] = rho[j], rho[i]
    for i in swapped:
        j = (i ^ first_bit) | second_bit
        for row in rho:
            row[i], row[j] = row[j], row[i]


def _apply_controlled(
    rho: list[list[complex]], control: int, target: int, size: int, matrix
) -> None:
    """Apply ``rho -> U rho U†`` for a controlled single-qubit unitary.

    ``U`` acts as the single-qubit *matrix* on *target* when the *control*
    bit is 1 and as the identity otherwise. Done as a left pass (rows whose
    control bit is set) followed by a right pass (columns whose control bit
    is set), which also covers the cross blocks between the two sectors.
    """
    cbit = 1 << control
    tbit = 1 << target
    g00, g01, g10, g11 = matrix
    h00, h01 = g00.conjugate(), g01.conjugate()
    h10, h11 = g10.conjugate(), g11.conjugate()
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, tbit):
        if not (i0 & cbit):
            continue
        i1 = i0 | tbit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j in range(size):
            m0 = row0[j]
            m1 = row1[j]
            row0[j] = g00 * m0 + g01 * m1
            row1[j] = g10 * m0 + g11 * m1
    for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, tbit):
        if not (j0 & cbit):
            continue
        j1 = j0 | tbit
        for i in range(size):
            row = rho[i]
            m0 = row[j0]
            m1 = row[j1]
            row[j0] = m0 * h00 + m1 * h01
            row[j1] = m0 * h10 + m1 * h11


def _amplitude_damping(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, gamma: float) -> None:
    bit = 1 << qubit
    scale = math.sqrt(1.0 - gamma)
    damped = 1.0 - gamma
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            m11 = row1[j1]
            row0[j0] = row0[j0] + gamma * m11
            row0[j1] = scale * row0[j1]
            row1[j0] = scale * row1[j0]
            row1[j1] = damped * m11


def _phase_damping(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, gamma: float) -> None:
    bit = 1 << qubit
    factor = 1.0 - gamma
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            row0[j1] = factor * row0[j1]
            row1[j0] = factor * row1[j0]


def _bit_flip(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, p: float) -> None:
    bit = 1 << qubit
    keep = 1.0 - p
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            m00 = row0[j0]
            m01 = row0[j1]
            m10 = row1[j0]
            m11 = row1[j1]
            row0[j0] = keep * m00 + p * m11
            row0[j1] = keep * m01 + p * m10
            row1[j0] = keep * m10 + p * m01
            row1[j1] = keep * m11 + p * m00


def _depolarizing(rho: list[list[complex]], qubit: int, size: int, p: float) -> None:
    bit = 1 << qubit
    keep = 1.0 - p
    half = p * 0.5
    for i0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
        i1 = i0 | bit
        row0 = rho[i0]
        row1 = rho[i1]
        for j0 in _basis_offsets(size, bit):
            j1 = j0 | bit
            m00 = row0[j0]
            m11 = row1[j1]
            mixed = half * (m00 + m11)
            row0[j0] = keep * m00 + mixed
            row1[j1] = keep * m11 + mixed
            row0[j1] = keep * row0[j1]
            row1[j0] = keep * row1[j0]


_CHANNELS = {
    "amplitude_damping": _amplitude_damping,
    "phase_damping": _phase_damping,
    "bit_flip": _bit_flip,
    "depolarizing": _depolarizing,
}


def evolve_density_matrix(program: Program, noise: dict[str, float]) -> list[list[complex]]:
    """Evolve and return the full final density matrix (row major).

    This is the same gate/noise evolution as :func:`simulate_density_matrix`
    but returns the complete matrix rather than only its diagonal. Noise
    evolution is deterministic and consumes no randomness; measurements do
    not collapse the state, matching the state-vector path.
    """
    n = program.num_qubits
    size = 1 << n
    rho = [[0j] * size for _ in range(size)]
    rho[0][0] = 1 + 0j

    for op in program.operations:
        if op.kind == "measure":
            continue
        spec = op.spec
        if op.kind == "cx":
            _apply_cx(rho, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], size)
        elif op.kind == "swap":
            _apply_swap(rho, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], size)
        elif spec.is_controlled:
            # cz and the controlled angle rotations embed the gate's one
            # registered target unitary on the target when control is 1.
            matrix = controlled_target_unitary(op.kind, op.params)
            _apply_controlled(rho, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], size, matrix)
        else:
            _apply_single_qubit(
                rho, op.targets[0], size, single_qubit_unitary(op.kind, op.params)
            )
        for qubit in sorted(set(op.targets)):
            for channel in CHANNEL_ORDER:
                probability = noise.get(channel)
                if probability:
                    _CHANNELS[channel](rho, qubit, size, probability)

    return rho


def simulate_density_matrix(program: Program, noise: dict[str, float]) -> list[float]:
    """Evolve the density matrix under all gates and noise channels.

    Returns the diagonal of the final density matrix (measurement
    probabilities per basis state). Measurements do not collapse the state,
    matching the state-vector path. Noise evolution is deterministic and
    consumes no randomness.
    """
    rho = evolve_density_matrix(program, noise)
    return [row[i].real for i, row in enumerate(rho)]

"""CLI-independent simulation application core.

Both the command line (``simulate``, ``probabilities`` and
``verify-samples``) and the Python DSL (:class:`~quantum_circuit.circuit.Circuit`)
prepare and validate their own inputs, then delegate here for the actual
work: state evolution, measurement probability aggregation, deterministic
sampling and canonical success-payload assembly.

This module never imports :mod:`quantum_circuit.cli` and performs no file,
standard input, environment or standard stream access. It receives only a
validated :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.Program` together with already
validated sampling parameters and a canonical noise model (as produced by
:func:`quantum_circuit.noise.validate_noise_model` /
:func:`quantum_circuit.noise.parse_noise_model`); failures intrinsic to a
simulation are reported as :class:`SimulationError`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

from .noise import MAX_NOISE_QUBITS, simulate_density_matrix
from .openqasm import Program
from .simulator import (
    measurement_probabilities,
    sample_counts,
    sample_counts_from_probabilities,
    simulate_state_vector,
)

# Probabilities are reported in full; entries this close to 0 are omitted
# and entries this close to 1 are reported as exactly 1. Reported values
# sum to within 1e-12 of 1.
PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE = 1e-15
PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE = 1e-15


class SimulationError(Exception):
    """The prepared circuit cannot be simulated (``simulation_error``).

    The only current case is a noisy circuit beyond the density-matrix
    qubit limit; command-line callers map it to exit code 3.
    """


def noisy_qubit_limit_error(num_qubits: int) -> SimulationError:
    return SimulationError(
        f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
        f"got {num_qubits}"
    )


def snap_probability(value: float) -> float | None:
    """Snap one probability for deterministic output.

    Returns ``None`` when the entry is omitted (magnitude at most
    ``1e-15``), ``1.0`` when it is within ``1e-15`` of 1, and otherwise a
    finite ``float`` clamped to ``(0, 1)`` so simulation round-off can
    never produce an out-of-range value.
    """
    if abs(value) <= PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE:
        return None
    if abs(1.0 - value) <= PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE:
        return 1.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, float(value)))


def evolve_basis_probabilities(
    program: Program, noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
) -> list[float]:
    """Evolve *program* and return per-basis-state measurement probabilities.

    Without a noise model the final state vector is evolved (the parser
    caps registers at the 20-qubit limit) and amplitudes are squared; with
    one the density matrix is evolved (at most :data:`~quantum_circuit.noise.MAX_NOISE_QUBITS`
    qubits) and its diagonal returned. Raises :class:`SimulationError` when
    a noisy circuit exceeds the density-matrix limit.
    """
    if noise_model is None:
        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
        return [abs(amplitude) ** 2 for amplitude in state]
    if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
        raise noisy_qubit_limit_error(program.num_qubits)
    return simulate_density_matrix(program, noise_model)


def probability_payload(
    program: Program,
    basis_probabilities: list[float],
    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Build the deterministic ``probabilities`` success payload.

    The aggregated classical distribution is renormalized by its total
    first, mirroring the normalization the sampling path applies to basis
    probabilities, so simulation round-off (notably density-matrix drift)
    cannot move the reported sum away from 1.
    """
    aggregated = measurement_probabilities(program, basis_probabilities)
    total = math.fsum(aggregated.values())
    probabilities: dict[str, float] = {}
    for key, value in aggregated.items():
        normalized = value / total if total else value
        snapped = snap_probability(normalized)
        if snapped is not None:
            probabilities[key] = snapped

    if noise_model is None:
        return {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
            "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
            "probabilities": probabilities,
        }
    return {
        "schema_version": 2,
        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
        "noise_model": noise_model,
        "probabilities": probabilities,
    }


def run_probabilities(
    program: Program, noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Evolve *program* and assemble its ``probabilities`` payload."""
    basis_probabilities = evolve_basis_probabilities(program, noise_model)
    return probability_payload(program, basis_probabilities, noise_model)


def run_simulation(
    program: Program,
    shots: int,
    seed: int,
    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Evolve a prepared circuit and sample it (the ``simulate`` payload).

    Sampling draws from a fresh RNG seeded by *seed*, so equal arguments
    produce equal results and no random state is shared between calls.
    Raises :class:`SimulationError` when a noisy circuit exceeds the
    density-matrix qubit limit.
    """
    if noise_model is None:
        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
        counts = sample_counts(program, state, shots, seed)
        return {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "shots": shots,
            "seed": seed,
            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
            "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
            "counts": counts,
        }
    if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
        raise noisy_qubit_limit_error(program.num_qubits)
    probabilities = simulate_density_matrix(program, noise_model)
    counts = sample_counts_from_probabilities(program, probabilities, shots, seed)
    return {
        "schema_version": 2,
        "shots": shots,
        "seed": seed,
        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
        "noise_model": noise_model,
        "counts": counts,
    }

1	"""Single authoritative source of quantum-gate semantics.
2	
3	Every other module that deals with gates reads the definitions it needs
4	from here instead of maintaining its own name lists or matrices:
5	
6	* the OpenQASM parser (:mod:`quantum_circuit.openqasm`) and the Python DSL
7	  (:mod:`quantum_circuit.circuit`) learn gate names, operand counts,
8	  parameter rules and operand orientation from :data:`GATE_SPECS` and build
9	  immutable :class:`Operation` values only through this module;
10	* the state-vector simulator (:mod:`quantum_circuit.simulator`), the
11	  density-matrix path (:mod:`quantum_circuit.noise`) and the unitary mode
12	  all take their 2x2 unitary expressions from :func:`rotation_matrix` /
13	  :func:`single_qubit_unitary` / :func:`controlled_target_unitary`, so a
14	  gate has one mathematical definition on every path;
15	* the optimizer (:mod:`quantum_circuit.optimizer`) uses the same registry
16	  for inverse pairs, self-inverse gates, the swap symmetry and the
17	  ``2*pi``/``4*pi`` rotation periods;
18	* resource estimation (:mod:`quantum_circuit.estimation`) uses the fixed
19	  gate-count orders below.
20	
21	This module is a dependency leaf: it imports only the standard library and
22	never imports the parser, simulator or command-line layers. Nothing here is
23	exported from the package root; gate semantics remain an internal contract.
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import cmath
29	import math
30	from dataclasses import dataclass
31	from types import MappingProxyType
32	from typing import Mapping
33	
34	# Operand shapes.
35	SINGLE_QUBIT = "single"
36	CONTROLLED = "controlled"
37	SWAP = "swap"
38	
39	# Rotation periodicity (see :class:`GateSpec.rotation_period`).
40	ROTATION_PERIOD = 2.0 * math.pi
41	CONTROLLED_ROTATION_PERIOD = 4.0 * math.pi
42	
43	_SQRT1_2 = 2.0**-0.5
44	
45	
46	@dataclass(frozen=True)
47	class GateSpec:
48	    """Immutable semantic definition of one supported gate.
49	
50	    Attributes:
51	        name: canonical OpenQASM gate name.
52	        style: :data:`SINGLE_QUBIT` (one operand), :data:`CONTROLLED`
53	            (``(control, target)`` operands, the gate acts on *target* when
54	            *control* is 1) or :data:`SWAP` (two unordered operands).
55	        parameterized: whether the gate takes exactly one angle parameter.
56	        axis: rotation axis ``"x"``/``"y"``/``"z"`` for the rotation gates,
57	            otherwise ``None``.
58	        unitary: the constant 2x2 unitary ``(g00, g01, g10, g11)`` of a
59	            non-parameterized single-qubit gate, or the unitary embedded on
60	            the target of a non-parameterized controlled gate (``cx``/``cz``).
61	        phase_factor: for a diagonal single-qubit gate, the eigenvalue by
62	            which the ``|1>`` amplitude is multiplied; otherwise ``None``.
63	        inverse_name: name of the inverse gate when a distinct one exists.
64	        self_inverse: whether two adjacent applications on the same qubits
65	            cancel.
66	        symmetric: whether the two operands are unordered (only ``swap``).
67	    """
68	
69	    name: str
70	    style: str
71	    parameterized: bool = False
72	    axis: str | None = None
73	    unitary: tuple[complex, complex, complex, complex] | None = None
74	    phase_factor: complex | None = None
75	    inverse_name: str | None = None
76	    self_inverse: bool = False
77	    symmetric: bool = False
78	
79	    @property
80	    def num_operands(self) -> int:
81	        """Number of qubit operands a valid application must carry."""
82	        return 1 if self.style == SINGLE_QUBIT else 2
83	
84	    @property
85	    def is_controlled(self) -> bool:
86	        """True for directed gates whose first operand is the control."""
87	        return self.style == CONTROLLED
88	
89	    @property

91	        """Angle period of a rotation gate, or ``None`` for fixed gates.

93	        Single-qubit rotations are ``2*pi`` periodic; controlled rotations
94	        are only ``4*pi`` periodic because a ``2*pi`` shift changes the
95	        control-1 block alone and is not a global phase of the controlled
96	        unitary.
97	        """
98	        if self.axis is None:
99	            return None
100	        return (
101	            CONTROLLED_ROTATION_PERIOD
102	            if self.style == CONTROLLED
103	            else ROTATION_PERIOD
104	        )
105	
106	    def target_unitary(
107	        self, params: tuple[float, ...] = ()
108	    ) -> tuple[complex, complex, complex, complex]:
109	        """The 2x2 unitary acting on the gate's target qubit.
110	
111	        For a single-qubit gate this is its full unitary; for a controlled
112	        gate it is the unitary embedded on the target when the control is 1.
113	        Parameterized rotations evaluate their (single) angle from *params*.
114	        """

256	SCHEMA_V3_GATES = frozenset(GATE_ORDER_V3) - frozenset(GATE_ORDER_V2)
